messages:
alex: quick async check-in — pushed kernel change that switches to adaptive micro-batching on canary (PR #4392). ran basic perf harness, saw 8% p99 regression for short seqs. posting what I did / blockers / plan for today

jane: thanks — can you paste the failing log snippet? is it a scheduling stall or KV-related?

alex: log snippet from canary run:
```
[2026-02-18 09:12:43] batcher: scheduling window=3ms, batch_size=6
[2026-02-18 09:12:43] kernel: launch gpu kernel lat=0.74ms
[2026-02-18 09:12:44] kv_cache: miss_rate spike -> 0.27, eviction_count=120
[2026-02-18 09:12:44] kernel: p99=24.1ms (+8% vs baseline)
```
seems correlated with KV miss bursts when adaptive creates slightly larger microbatches for short seq traffic.

kai: hmm, that sounds like the adaptive window is letting small bursts coalesce and then thrashes cache. did you try lowering BATCHER_MAX_WINDOW_MS?

alex: not yet, i want to validate across the perf harness (short/med/long seq mixes). current canary config: `BATCHER_MAX_WINDOW_MS=5, ADAPTIVE=true, TARGET_BATCH=8` — I can try `BATCHER_MAX_WINDOW_MS=2` and re-run.

devin: also consider increasing KV prefetch limit for short sequences — we saw similar behavior in the A/B from Dec where miss spikes drove kernel stalls. maybe `KV_PREFETCH_TOP_K=64` instead of 16.

alex: good call. i'll run a 24hr sweep with (A) window=2 + prefetch=16, (B) window=5 + prefetch=64, (C) window=2 + prefetch=64 and compare. hooking up grafana panels: /d/redwood/runtime_kv?orgId=1&panelId=7 (will paste after runs)

tj: i can take PR review once you add a changelog entry and an integration test that fakes KV miss bursts. ping me when ready.

alex: will add test that injects synthetic misses at NTP. also adding a small perf test: `./tools/microbench --cases short,medium,long --iters 1000 --log csv` and uploading CSV to the PR. expecting to have results by EOD.

jane: FYI ops: if this looks like it needs a rollback, what's the quick rollback path? cc @ops

build-bot: CI for PR #4392 — unit: ✅, integration: running (2/3), e2e: queued

devin: one more thought — the kernel launch path can be slightly sensitive to batch_size variance; if adaptive oscillates, we might see tail effects. consider hysteresis (only change batch size if delta >= 2).

alex: noted — adding hysteresis ticket to the PR description. blocker: need to reproduce consistent miss spike locally; if I can't, i'll ask infra to re-run canary with traffic replay.

kai: if you need a quick local repro, i have a small script that replays our short-seq poisson trace. i'll DM it.

alex: perfect, please DM. thanks everyone. summary: what I did: pushed adaptive microbatch change to canary, collected baseline; blocker: KV miss bursts causing p99 regression; today: run sweep A/B/C, add test & changelog, request review from tj, and attach grafana + CSV to PR. :thumbsup:
